haiku-low.q1: MySQL first: commit the change and its pending_sync row together, then apply it to Postgres. If Postgres fails, the user's request still succeeds; the sweeper repairs Postgres later.
haiku-low.q2: Only if the incoming row's version is higher than the existing row's version, and no tombstone exists for that id. Otherwise the copy is skipped.
haiku-low.q3: Every instance must show dual_mysql_primary in app_flag_value. Instances can disagree on flags for up to 30 seconds after a change.
haiku-low.q4: Batches of at most 2,000 rows, and before each batch it waits while MySQL replica lag is above 5 seconds.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: backfill finished and a comparer pass with zero mismatches. Source-of-truth switch: 3 days at 100% reads with a clean comparer, then the switch procedure.
haiku-low.q6: The pending_sync row in the source-of-truth database, committed with the change. The sweeper copies the current row or tombstone to the other database and removes the id.
haiku-low.q7: Tombstones block re-creation: the version rule skips any copy whose id has a tombstone, and tombstones are never deleted.
haiku-low.q8: Progress is last_id in Postgres backfill_progress, saved in the same transaction as each batch copy, so it matches copied rows. Restart resumes from last_id. Stopping point: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q9: The comparer scans all rows of both tables by id, both directions. Each mismatched id is added to pending_sync, and the sweeper repairs it.
haiku-low.q10: Paused mode returns 503 to writes until all instances show paused plus 5 seconds. If the switch is not done 45 seconds after step 1, the flag reverts to the previous mode.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres assigns ids via its sequence, set to MySQL max id + 1 while writes are frozen. After rollback, MySQL accepts explicit ids and advances AUTO_INCREMENT, so no collisions.
haiku-low.q12: MySQL keeps receiving every write via dual writes. Rollback runs the switch procedure to dual_mysql_primary. The window lasts at least 14 days; dropping the MySQL table at step 9 ends it.

sonnet.q1: The source of truth (MySQL) is committed first, with the pending-list insert in the same transaction; then the change is applied to Postgres with the version rule. If the Postgres part fails the error is ignored and the user's request succeeds; the sweeper repairs it later.
sonnet.q2: Only if the row is missing, or the existing row's version is lower than the incoming version; and the copy is skipped if a tombstone exists for that id.
sonnet.q3: app_flag_value must show every instance on dual_mysql_primary. Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds (flag refresh interval).
sonnet.q4: The backfill runs from the MySQL replica, uses a single worker, batches of at most 2,000 rows, and before each batch waits while replica lag exceeds 5 seconds.
sonnet.q5: Reads: backfill finished and the comparer completed one full pass with zero mismatches, then staged 1, 10, 50, 100 percent. Source of truth: 3+ days at 100 percent reads with the comparer still running and clean.
sonnet.q6: A row in the pending_sync(user_id) table, kept in the source-of-truth database (MySQL at this stage), inserted in the same transaction as the change. The sweeper reads the current row/tombstone from the source of truth, copies it with the version rule, and removes the id from the list.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones: an erased id has a tombstone (inserted in the delete transaction, never deleted), and the version rule makes any copy be skipped if a tombstone exists for that id.
sonnet.q8: In the one-row table backfill_progress in Postgres, as last_id (highest id of the batch). It is saved in the same Postgres transaction as the batch's copy, so they stay consistent. It stops when it has copied all existing rows (backfill finished); the document does not state a more precise stop condition.
sonnet.q9: The comparer scans all rows of both tables by id in both directions (skipping pending ids and rows changed in the last 60 s, checked next pass). Each mismatch id is added to the pending list and the sweeper repairs it.
sonnet.q10: write_mode is set to paused (retryable 503 for writes); wait until app_flag_value shows every instance on paused plus 5 seconds, drain the pending list (and set the sequence for the Postgres switch), then set the new mode. If step 4 hasn't happened 45 seconds after step 1, the flag is set back to the previous mode and investigated (worst case about 75 s per instance).
sonnet.q11: A Postgres sequence assigns ids, set to MySQL's current max id + 1 during the paused switch. On rollback, MySQL accepts explicit ids and moves its AUTO_INCREMENT past them, so no id fix is needed.
sonnet.q12: MySQL receives a copy of every write (dual_pg_primary), staying in sync for at least 14 days. Rollback is running the same switching procedure to dual_mysql_primary. The option ends when MySQL's table is dropped in step 9 (pg_only, backup, drop), after which there is no rollback.
